name: Positive Paucal a few and a little
pattern: NP[Det:a few + plural count nominal, or Det:a little + non-count nominal]

entry.name: Positive Paucal a few and a little
entry.pattern: NP[Det:a few + plural count nominal, or Det:a little + non-count nominal]

1.definition: Presents a small quantity as a positive amount.

projection.target: A little asserts some available time. Bare little favours an inadequate-amount reading and patterns differently in environments sensitive to negative orientation.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: A few and a little
curious.summary: A few and a little present a small quantity as a positive amount.
curious.body: In We still have a little time, the speaker presents the time as available. A little goes with a non-count word like time, and a few goes with a plural count word, as in a few minutes. This dictionary contrasts a little with plain little. Bare little favours a reading where the amount is inadequate, and it behaves differently in some settings that are sensitive to negative orientation.
curious.try: Compare We have a little time with We have little time. Which one presents the time as available?

teacher.summary: Contrasts a few and a little, which present a small amount as positive, with bare little.
teacher.explain: The pattern is a determiner a few with a plural count nominal, or a little with a non-count nominal, presenting a small quantity as a positive amount. A little asserts some available time. Bare little favours an inadequate-amount reading and patterns differently in environments sensitive to negative orientation. This dictionary files the pattern as a specialization of the noun phrase with a determiner and relates it to an absolute negator determinative. It is provisional, with medium confidence.
teacher.terms: This dictionary calls this positive paucal, paucal meaning a small number, in contrast with bare little.

contrasts.text: We still have a little time.

watch_for: A learner might use a little with a plural count noun, when the pattern pairs a little with a non-count nominal.
A learner might read bare little as the same as a little, when bare little favours an inadequate-amount reading.
teacher.activity: Students write sentences about their week using a few with plural nouns and a little with non-count nouns, then swap and check that each pairing fits.

child.hook: If you have a few minutes, is there time to play?
child.explain: A few and a little name a small amount. We still have a little time. We still have a few minutes. A few goes with things you can count.

examples.text: We still have a little time.
We still have a few minutes.

child.play: Look in your pencil case. Say what you have a few of and what you have a little of.

checked.note: Fixed: child explanation no longer says the expressions mean 'you have some' (availability comes from the sentence; the entry gives a quantity meaning); curious summary no longer says 'not as too little'; try question asks which presents the time as available, matching the entry. Dismissed: none.
